summary: Master third-party and supply chain cyber risk with ISO/IEC 27001, NIST SP 800-161, and FAIR models. Secure vendors, mitigate breaches, and ensure compliance. R
lede: Third-party and supply chain cyber risk management helps security, risk, procurement and compliance professionals identify and address threats across vendor relationships. The course covers mapping vendor ecosystems, assessing security controls, building risk registers, modeling supply chain threats, prioritizing risks by likelihood and business impact, drafting risk-transfer clauses, monitoring vendors, and planning responses to vendor breaches.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for managing security risks across external vendor ecosystems and supply chains.
outcomes: NIST SP 800-161 Supply Chain Risk Management
modules: Foundations of Third-Party and Supply Chain Cyber Risk
Frameworks and Standards for Vendor Risk Management
Assessing and Quantifying Third-Party Cyber Risk
Contractual Risk Transfer and Legal Compliance
Continuous Monitoring and AI-Driven Vendor Oversight
Supply Chain Threat Modeling and Mitigation Strategies
Incident Response for Vendor and Supply Chain Breaches
Integrating Third-Party Risk into Business Strategy and Reporting
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Participants should have at least 2-3 years of experience in IT security, risk management, or supply chain operations. A working knowledge of basic cybersecurity concepts (e.g., firewalls, encryption, malware) and familiarity with risk management principles (e.g., likelihood, impact) is highly recommended. No coding or programming skills are required, but an understanding of enterprise IT infrastructure is beneficial. This is an intermediate-level course designed for practitioners ready to apply frameworks to real-world vendor scenarios.
